prompt.context: Our client is Healthy Foods Co., a wholesaler serving a variety of clients with food products. The client is profitable but they want you to help them find revenue growth opportunities from their current business.
prompt.question: How can we help Healthy Foods Co. drive their revenue growth?

clarifying_info.a: The client serves various customer categories, which are shown in Exhibit 1.

clarifying_info.q: What are the sensitivities or priorities of the client's customers?
clarifying_info.a: Customer sensitivities ranked highest to lowest: price, convenient delivery, help with location planning, help with menu, website development, inventory management, help with management optimization.
The client is one of the market leaders and is not losing market share.

exhibits.title: Total Market Revenues by Customer Type
exhibits.shows: A pie or bar chart showing revenues broken down by customer type: independent restaurants, chain restaurants, hospitals, school cafeterias, grocery stores, and other.
exhibits.data: Customer categories: Independent restaurants (largest slice), Chain restaurants, Hospitals, School cafeterias, Grocery stores, Other.

exhibits.title: Client's Share of Wallet by Customer Type
exhibits.shows: A chart plotting share of wallet (0-80%) for different customer types labeled A, B, C, and X (A=highest profitability, X=lowest), indicating whether the client is the primary supplier or one of many suppliers for each.
exhibits.data: Y-axis: Share of Wallet 0-80%; Customer types: A (highest profit), B, C, X (lowest profit); Two categories shown: Client is Primary Supplier vs. Client is One of Many.

exhibits.title: Wallet Size vs. Share of Wallet for Smaller-Revenue-Generating Customer Categories
exhibits.shows: A scatter plot with share of wallet (%) on the x-axis (0-60%) and wallet size ($M) on the y-axis (0-600), plotting the smaller-revenue-generating customer categories: hospitals, hotels, school cafeterias, grocery stores, and chain restaurants.
exhibits.data: X-axis: Share of Wallet 0-60%; Y-axis: Wallet Size $0-600M; Data points: Hospitals (high wallet size, low share of wallet), Hotels (high wallet size, low share of wallet), School cafeterias (mid wallet, mid share), Grocery stores (mid wallet, higher share), Chain restaurants (lower wallet, higher share).

framework: Identify current customer mix and revenue contribution by customer type (Exhibit 1)
Analyze share of wallet across customer types to understand where the client is already dominant vs. underpenetrated (Exhibit 2)
Prioritize customer segments for growth by mapping wallet size against current share of wallet — target large wallets with low share (Exhibit 3)
Develop targeted strategies to increase share of wallet in the highest-potential segments (hospitals and hotels)

questions.prompt: Which customer types generate the most revenue today, and what does that imply for growth opportunities?
questions.guidance: The candidate should use Exhibit 1 to identify that independent restaurants are the largest revenue category, followed by a number of other customer types (chain restaurants, hospitals, school cafeterias, grocery stores, other) with similar but smaller contributions. The candidate should note that while independent restaurants are the largest segment, growth potential there depends on share of wallet and room to expand.

questions.prompt: What is the client's share of wallet across different customer types, and what does this tell us about growth opportunities?
questions.guidance: Using Exhibit 2, the candidate should recognize that the client's share of wallet is already high (client is primary supplier) for the highest-revenue and highest-profitability customers. This means there is limited room to grow revenue from those segments. The key insight is that growth opportunity lies in the smaller-revenue-generating customer categories where the client is currently 'one of many' and share of wallet is lower.

questions.prompt: Among the smaller-revenue-generating customer types, which ones represent the largest growth opportunity?
questions.guidance: Using Exhibit 3, the candidate should apply the prioritization logic: the best growth opportunity is in customer segments with a large wallet size AND low current share of wallet (i.e., the client is underpenetrated in a large market). The candidate should identify hospitals and hotels as the top candidates — they have very large wallet sizes ($400-600M range) but low share of wallet (~10-20%). The candidate should then suggest ways to better serve these segments based on their sensitivities (e.g., convenient delivery, inventory management, pricing).

math.setup: Prioritization framework: Growth opportunity = Wallet Size x (1 - Current Share of Wallet). Hospitals and hotels have large wallets (~$400-600M) with low share (~10-20%), meaning the addressable upside is $320-540M per segment if share of wallet could be significantly improved.
steps: Hospitals: Wallet ~$500M, share of wallet ~10-15% => addressable opportunity ~$425-450M
Hotels: Wallet ~$400-500M, share of wallet ~10-20% => addressable opportunity ~$320-450M
Compare to chain restaurants: Wallet ~$200M, share ~40-50% => addressable opportunity ~$100-120M
math.answer: Hospitals and hotels have the highest revenue growth potential due to their large wallet sizes combined with the client's currently low share of wallet in those segments.

brainstorming.prompt: What specific actions could Healthy Foods Co. take to increase its share of wallet with hospitals and hotels?

categories.name: Pricing & Contracting
ideas: Offer volume-based discounts to large institutional buyers
Develop long-term supply contracts to lock in hospital and hotel accounts
Create bundled pricing for multiple product categories

categories.name: Delivery & Logistics
ideas: Offer more flexible or frequent delivery schedules to match institutional needs
Provide just-in-time delivery to reduce clients' inventory burden
Develop dedicated logistics tracks for high-volume institutional clients

categories.name: Product & Menu Support
ideas: Provide menu planning assistance tailored to hospital dietary/nutritional requirements
Offer specialized healthy food product lines suited to hospital patients
Assist hotels with seasonal menu development and food trend guidance

categories.name: Relationship & Service
ideas: Assign dedicated account managers to hospital and hotel accounts
Offer inventory management tools or software integration
Provide staff training on product usage and food safety

categories.name: Marketing & Awareness
ideas: Target procurement and food service directors at hospitals and hotel chains
Leverage case studies from existing hospital/hotel clients
Participate in industry trade shows for hospitality and healthcare food service

recommendation: The largest revenue growth opportunities for Healthy Foods Co. lie in the hospital and hotel customer segments, which have large food purchasing budgets ($400-600M wallet size) but low current share of wallet for the client (~10-20%).

The client should focus on increasing penetration in these two segments by addressing their specific needs — particularly convenient delivery, pricing competitiveness, and inventory support — to convert from being 'one of many' suppliers to becoming the primary supplier.
risks: Hospitals and hotels may have long-term contracts with existing suppliers that are difficult to displace
Serving institutional clients at scale may require operational investments in logistics and dedicated service capacity
Price sensitivity may compress margins if the client needs to discount to win new accounts
next_steps: Conduct in-depth customer research with hospital and hotel procurement teams to understand current pain points and supplier selection criteria
Pilot an enhanced service offering (e.g., dedicated delivery schedule, inventory management support) with 2-3 hospital or hotel clients
Assess internal operational capacity to scale service delivery to institutional clients before pursuing broad outreach
